entry: Start. Two additions were asked for: multi-resolution silent sets, and spliced against unspliced reads for nuclei; nothing is to be published until Glymph is clearly ahead of CellBender. Where 0.3.2 stands against CellBender 0.4.0 (run 20261117-1342_glymph-cb040-bench): ahead on per-cell error (30 of 32 libraries), 10x removal, nuclei, Parse and speed; behind on BD Rhapsody removal by one point and on own counts kept (98.6% against 99.0% on the twelve libraries never used; 98.0% against 99.3% on xenografts); the level on very clean xenografts moves between runs; per-cell rank agreement in kidney tissue is low for both tools (0.38 and 0.37).

Reads for the splicing measurement. The nuclei mixture (NEAT-seq, GSE178707) has no deposited reads for its RNA library, so it cannot be used. The five kidney libraries were deposited as Cell Ranger alignment files; the SRA's public bucket serves them at about 12 MB/s per file, ENA at 1. The nuclei were aligned to a pre-mRNA reference (mm10-2.1.0_premrna): every read inside a gene carries the exonic tag, and reads that cross a splice junction got no gene at all, so they are in neither the files' gene counts nor the count matrix. Reads are therefore classified by position against a real exon annotation (10x mm10-2020-A): unspliced when 10 or more aligned bases lie outside every exon, otherwise exonic (called ambiguous in the tables). Script 51_bam_splice_counts.py, one process per chromosome.

Multi-resolution silent sets written (src/glymph/multires.py). Each cluster of the calibration is split into up to eight sub-clusters of about 40 cells or more. For each gene: entries far above what background explains mark carriers, and a group with fewer than three carriers (or 8% of its cells) is judged without them; if the cluster is above background, the one or two sub-clusters with the largest excess are set aside when they clearly express the gene, and the gene is silent for the rest if the rest is at background; a sub-cluster that holds far more of its parent's counts than its share of the background is not held to the gene. This replaces leaving whole cells out of the cluster sums. Also an option to build the clusters on principal components of the counts (the same in every run) in place of the model's latent space. Unit test on simulated tissue passes (a sub-population keeps its own genes, its siblings gain them, a doublet is ignored), as do all earlier tests. First round on the 23 development libraries: tree on latent clusters, tree on principal-component clusters, one resolution on principal-component clusters, two runs each.

Splicing signal checked against truth before any model code (kidney_nuc2). Molecule counts from the alignment file match the count matrix (ratio 1.023, correlation 0.9999). Unspliced share: 9% of the empty droplets' molecules, 29% of the cells'. For ten proximal-tubule marker genes: 4.4% unspliced in the empty droplets, 10.3% in the nuclei of other cell types (where they are background), 39.7% in tubule nuclei. So per gene the contrast is four to nine fold. As one number per cell it is weak: correlation with the genotype truth 0.31 among nuclei (Glymph 0.3.2: 0.26; CellBender 0.4.0: 0.22; the truth's own reliability allows 0.88), because a nucleus also keeps some of its own cytoplasm. Decision: use splicing per gene and per molecule, not as a per-cell total. The three whole-cell kidney libraries were aligned without introns (0.4 to 0.7% unspliced everywhere), so they carry no such information; their jobs were cancelled.

First round scored (15 development mixtures, 5 kidney libraries; 0.3.2 twice beside each variant twice). Clusters from principal components: two runs of the same code now differ by 0.06 to 0.11 points of cross-species removal on average and 0.35 to 0.65 at most (latent clusters: 1.1 to 1.9 on average, 5 to 17 at most). Accuracy with them, one resolution: removal 89.2% to 91.1%, per-cell error 0.0159 to 0.0154, rank agreement 0.69 to 0.71 (xeno_HSC_3 removal 72-75% to 88%, parse_hgmm_sub2 68% to 87%; parse_hgmm_sub1 83-88% to 77%; jurkat_32d error 0.010 to 0.012); kidney removed over truth 1.00 to 1.06 (kidney_rep3 1.05 to 1.22, kidney_rep1 0.84 to 0.92), tubule markers removed 86% to 89%. The level still depends on the clustering; it is now the same in every run. The first tree (sub-clusters set aside, isolated carriers) is worse than one resolution on the same clusters: BD mix 1 91.6% to 88.3%, six 10x mixtures 0.5 to 1.5 points lower, marker counts kept in their own cells on tissue lower (kidney_nuc3 99.8% to 98.0%, parse_bm_hfd 91% to 80%), kidney removed over truth 1.09. Two causes: a few doublets per sub-cluster are more than isolated carriers, so the other species' genes stop being silent there; and a gene that one sub-type expresses weakly becomes silent for it once two stronger ones are set aside.

Tree reworked so that it can only protect: the cluster's silent genes are found as in 0.3.2 (cells far above the fit left out of the sums), and a sub-cluster overrules its cluster for a gene that a quarter or more of its cells carry (three at least). The first tree stays as an option that is off. Clusters from principal components are the default.

First splicing round (first tree, latent clusters, two runs each): tubule markers removed from other cell types on kidney_nuc2 87-88% without splicing, 89-91% with it for the silent sets, 91% with both uses (CellBender 0.4.0: 96%); per-cell error unchanged. Its diagnostics showed a fault in the first version: the unspliced share of background inside cells was fitted on the count-silent genes and came out at 0.34 (median over informative genes), with the logit shift at 1.3 to 1.45 on nuc2 and at the upper bound of 3.0 on nuc3, where tubule markers in other cell types show 0.10. Checked by pooling gene and cell-type pairs by how little the cell type expresses the gene: even at 1 to 5% of the top cell type's rate the molecules are 68 to 86% unspliced where the empty droplets' are 37 to 49% and own expression 71 to 91%. So genes that are silent by their counts still hold nascent transcripts of the nucleus's own, and a background fitted on them takes that for background. The background's unspliced share is now the empty partitions' (shift 0); the fitted value is only reported. Second rounds submitted: the reworked tree on the 23 development libraries, twice; and on the two kidney nuclei libraries splicing off, for the output only, for the silent sets only, for both (twice), and for both with the fitted shift.

Can splicing alone measure how much of a cell type's RNA is background? No. With the unspliced share of each gene in the empty partitions and in its top cell type, the background share of a cell type's molecules follows by interpolation; summed over the informative genes (47% and 58% of the molecules) it gives 29% on both nuclei libraries, where the genotype truth is 40% (kidney_nuc2) and 19% (kidney_nuc3). Across the eight cell types of kidney_nuc2 it follows the truth with correlation 0.43 (Glymph 0.3.2: 0.88; CellBender 0.4.0: 0.58). The amount stays with the silent-gene fit; splicing is used per gene (which genes are silent where, which entries hold the background) and not for the level. Script: code/benchmark/diag_splice_amount.py.

Round M2 scored (23 development libraries, two runs): the tree that can only protect is neutral. Cross-species removal on the 15 mixtures 90.7 to 90.8% (clusters from principal components alone 91.1%, 0.3.2 89.0 to 89.4%, CellBender 0.4.0 83.4%), per-cell error 0.0156 (0.0154; CellBender 0.040), rank agreement 0.70 (0.71; 0.48), same-species removal 0.995 of expected (0.976; CellBender 0.62). Kidney: removed over truth 1.07, tubule markers removed from other cell types 88.3% (89.2%), kept in tubule cells 87.7%. Two runs differ by 0.10 points of removal on average. Kept as the default because it costs nothing here and is the safeguard for sub-types; it is not where accuracy comes from.

Round S2 scored (kidney nuclei, splicing with the unspliced share of background taken from the empty partitions): small and not consistent. kidney_nuc2, tubule markers removed from other cell types: 90.2% without splicing, 92.8% with splicing for the silent sets only, 89.8% for the output only, 88.7 to 88.8% with both, 93.1% with the fitted shift; CellBender 95.7% (which keeps 57% of those markers in tubule cells against 62 to 64% here, and has per-cell error 0.168 against 0.134 to 0.139). kidney_nuc3: 91.7% without, 91.7 to 92.8% with; removed over truth rises from 1.03 to 1.07 and per-cell error from 0.116 to 0.120. Splicing separates genes on average and not cell by cell or pair by pair with enough power; it stays in the code as an option that reads layers["unspliced"], and is not a source of accuracy so far.

Where the missed cross-species counts sit (code/benchmark/diag_unremoved.py, diag_cross_excess.py; hgmm_10k_v3, bd_hgmm_mix1, hgmm_1k_v3). (1) Genes at more than 10 times the ambient profile (reads of the cell's own gene aligned to the other genome: ribosomal and mitochondrial RNA, processed pseudogenes; 3 to 20% of the cross-species counts) are left alone by Glymph and by CellBender alike (both keep 93 to 97%), so they lower every tool's score equally. (2) On genes within 1.5 times the ambient profile CellBender removes 95.6 to 99.8% and Glymph 93.7 to 98.1%; on genes at 1.5 to 3 times, 87 to 93% against 80 to 86%. That is the gap to close on 10x and BD cell-line mixtures.

Cause found with a dump of the silent test (GLYMPH_DEBUG_DUMP, code/benchmark/diag_silent_pairs.py): the fit puts the swapped fraction at zero on all three mixtures (theta: hgmm_10k_v3 0.90, 0.55, 0; bd_hgmm_mix1 0.17, 1.16, 0; hgmm_1k_v3 1.13, 1.10, 0), where a fit of the same three amounts on the cross-species counts of the pure clusters gives 0.88, 0, 0.0161; 0.35, 0.44, 0.0045; 1.32, 0.26, 0.0034. The fitted background is 14, 14 and 28% short, and the misfit follows log(average cell profile over soup profile) with correlation 0.92, 0.51, 0.45: Malat1 and mitochondrial genes sit at 2.3 to 3 times the fit in every human cluster of hgmm_10k_v3 and so fail the silent test (only 60% of the cross-species counts of those clusters are on silent genes). With the right amounts 93 to 94% of the cross-species counts pass the test instead of 80 to 88%. Reason: summed over a cell's silent genes, depth-proportional ambient background and swapped background cannot be told apart, and the 3% lean against the swapped term then sends it to zero.

0.4.0.dev5, two additions. (a) Gene contrast for the swapped fraction (exclusion._swap_shape, option swap_contrast): the split of the depth-proportional background between soup profile and average cell profile is searched over eleven proportions, and the one at which the most candidate pairs lie on the lowest ridge wins; the per-cell fit then finds two amounts. A direct fit in three groups of genes was tried first and settled at about half the true value whatever the solver (the genes that would show a larger swapped fraction lie above the ridge while it is too small, so the fit confirms its start); on simulated tissue the search gives 0.0235, 0, 0.0532 for true 0.03, 0.005, 0.06 (before: about zero). (b) A level shared across clusters (multires.shared_level, options silent_factor_max = 3, factor_budget): per gene, the clusters that do not express it are ordered by observed over fitted, and the lowest group that agrees on one multiple (two clusters or more, 10 expected counts, between a third and three times the fit) makes the gene silent there at that multiple; the multiple is also the gene's background level in every other cell (model.log_phi). Even with the right amounts the cross-species counts sit at 0.6 to 1.8 times the fit gene by gene (10th to 90th percentile), which one cluster cannot tell from expression and several clusters can. This is the measured background profile proposed on 2026-11-18, reached through the multi-resolution route.

0.4.0.dev5 checked on three mixtures before the full round (share of all cross-species counts removed, no gene masked; previous round; CellBender 0.4.0): hgmm_10k_v3 97.1% (95.7%; 95.9%), with 99.2% against 98.1% on genes within 1.5 times the ambient profile and 91.8% against 86.8% on genes at 1.5 to 3 times; hgmm_1k_v3 86.7% (85.9%; 86.8%); bd_hgmm_mix1 84.4% (84.7%; 85.4%). The swapped fraction now comes out at 0.0098, 0.0008 and 0.0035 (cross-species counts: 0.0164, 0.0033, 0.0045). Round M3 submitted on the 23 development libraries: both additions (two runs), each alone, the shared level for the silent sets only, and both with a false-positive allowance of 0.2%.

What is left after dev5, by what the silent test said (code/benchmark/diag_left_by_mask.py). hgmm_10k_v3: 92% of the cross-species counts are on silent genes and 99.7% of those are removed; what is left is ribosomal and mitochondrial RNA aligned to the other genome (RNA18S5, RNA28S5, mt-Rnr2, Gm42418), which no tool should remove. bd_hgmm_mix1: silent genes 78% of the counts, 99.8% removed; the rest is the mis-aligned genes (Gm42418 alone 25,000 counts) and one cause that is Glymph's: about 80 mouse cells with 6% human RNA form a cluster of their own, every human gene counts as expressed there, and their human counts stay (MT-CO1 539 of 573 left).

0.4.0.dev6 and dev7: a cluster that is a larger cluster plus background-like RNA takes that cluster's silent genes (option superpose). The rule that 0.3.2 applies to single cells, applied to clusters and sub-clusters: on the larger cluster's silent genes the cluster holds at least three times its fitted background, at most a fifth of its counts, on 50 genes or more, in the proportions of the background (overlap at least 0.5). Its cells are then judged one by one as before. dev6 (tested only on the genes the cluster did not already have as silent) also joined two clean clusters of the same cell line on 0.05% of their counts, which is noise; dev7 tests the whole silent set and asks for three times the background. dev6 on the three mixtures: bd_hgmm_mix1 87.8% of all cross-species counts removed (CellBender 85.4%), 97.8% against 95.0% on genes within 3 times the ambient profile, human genes in mouse cells 98.9% against 93.4%; hgmm_10k_v3 97.6% against 95.9% (99.3% against 97.5%). On simulated tissue 150 cells with 10% extra RNA get their own type's silent genes (98% of the other types' genes silent for them, 32% without the rule) and the rarest true cell type keeps its set (tests/test_superpose.py).

0.4.0.dev7 on six mixtures before the full round (share of all cross-species counts removed, no gene masked; round M2; CellBender 0.4.0): bd_hgmm_mix1 88.0% (84.7%; 85.4%), hgmm_10k_v3 97.4% (95.7%; 95.9%), hgmm_1k_v3 86.9% (85.9%; 86.8%), xeno_HSC_1 86.3% (86.3%; 76.4%), jurkat_32d 95.5% (89.3%; 85.4%; its swapped fraction is read at 3.6% of depth, nine tenths of the depth-proportional background), neat_barnyard 65.2% (64.6%; 26.0%). Ahead of CellBender on all six. Clusters given a larger cluster's silent genes: two on bd_hgmm_mix1 (68 cells with 16% and 82 cells with 5.5% of their counts on the other species), two on hgmm_10k_v3, one on jurkat_32d, none on the others; whole populations of the other species are kept apart by the one-fifth limit (their share is 65 to 98%). Round M4 submitted: dev7 twice, allowance 0.2% and 0.1%, largest shared level 2, no tree; rounds M3 and M4 are scored together.

Rounds M3 and M4 scored (tables kept in metrics_rounds_3_4/ and generic_rounds_3_4/). What looked excellent on cell lines fails on tissue with genotype truth. Means over the 15 development mixtures and the 5 kidney libraries (round M2; gene contrast alone; plus the shared level = M3; plus background-like clusters = M4; CellBender 0.4.0): cross-species removal 90.7%; 91.2%; 91.6%; 91.1%; 83.4%. Libraries ahead of CellBender on removal 9; 12; 13; 14. Per-cell error on mixtures 0.0156; 0.0157; 0.0158; 0.0200; 0.040. Kidney, removed over truth 1.07; 1.08; 1.21; 1.39; 0.96. Kidney per-cell error 0.089; 0.092; 0.098; 0.108; 0.097. Kidney rank agreement 0.386; 0.384; 0.377; 0.301; 0.368.

The shared level is switched off (silent_factor_max = 1). It adds 2 points of removal on two 10x libraries, and on kidney_rep2 it removes 1.83 times the true background (1.25 without it; 1.37 when used for the silent sets only): the genes that sit at the same multiple of the fitted background in every cluster that does not express them are, in a kidney, genes that neighbouring cell types express weakly, and the multiple then also raises their budget in the tubule cells that express them. One cluster cannot tell expression from a gene-specific background level, and several clusters cannot either when the expression is uniform. The code and its test stay, documented as wrong for tissue.

The rule for background-like clusters is switched off (superpose = False). It cleans the dirty cells of bd_hgmm_mix1 (95.5% of cross-species counts removed with the usual genes masked, against 91.5% and CellBender's 92.6%), and it merges true cell types: xeno_HSC_3 lost 11 points (a population of 611 cells with 10% of its counts on another cluster's silent genes, at 94 times the background and match 0.79, is a cell type), parse_hgmm_sub2 got 2.0 times the expected same-species removal, kidney removed over truth rose to 1.15, 2.09 and 1.74 on the three whole-cell libraries, and a cell type's own markers were lost (kept on: pfc_ga22 35%, kidney_rep1 74%, parse_igvf_NOOZ 86%). The background on another cluster's silent genes has that cluster's neighbours' profile, so a cell type that differs from its neighbour by a tenth of its counts looks the same as dirty cells. The BD gap stays as a known limit: about 150 cells of 9,500 that carry 5 to 16% of the other species keep it.

Gene contrast for the swapped fraction, read on all 23 libraries (code/benchmark/show_fit_table.py): clear on 10x cell-line mixtures (thousands of candidate pairs; 60 to 90% of the depth-proportional background has the average cell profile; swapped fraction 0.7 to 1.5% of depth, 3.6% on jurkat_32d where the cross-species counts give 3.4%) and on nuclei (kidney_nuc2 and kidney_nuc3: all of it, 37% more pairs on the ridge; pfc_ga22 70%); nothing to split on whole-cell kidney and hgmm_10k_5pv2_ctrl (no depth-proportional part); noise on libraries with 100 to 250 pairs, where the best proportion followed 6 pairs in 104 and flipped parse_hgmm_sub2 from 87% to 66% removed. On nuclei the swapped fraction hit the bound of 5% of depth and the rest of the depth-proportional budget was dropped (kidney_nuc2 removed over truth 0.85, from 0.91). 0.4.0.dev8: the soup profile stays unless the best proportion puts clearly more pairs on the ridge (two standard deviations and 3%); the bound is 30% of depth (swap_cap) and what it takes goes back to the soup-profile term. Round M5: dev8 twice, and false-positive allowances of 0.3% and 0.2% (in round M3 0.2% gave same-species removal 0.88 of expected and native loss 0.06%, against 1.03 and 0.14% at 0.4%).

Open question raised by jurkat_32d: with the swapped fraction at 3.6% (right for the cross-species counts) the same-species removal is 1.36 times what the benchmark expects, and rank agreement falls from 0.82 to 0.78. The benchmark takes each cell's cross-species counts times the species split of the empty partitions; swapped molecules follow the split of the cells. code/benchmark/diag_species_split.py measures the split inside cells from both directions (human RNA in mouse cells against mouse RNA in human cells); queued.

Round M5 scored (0.4.0.dev8; tables in metrics_round_5/). Mixtures as with gene contrast alone (removal 91.5%, ahead of CellBender on 10 of 15, per-cell error 0.0158). Kidney nuclei worse, and the cause is the higher bound, not a bug: with up to 30% of depth allowed, the search put 14% (kidney_nuc2) and 13% (kidney_nuc3) of depth on the average nucleus profile, with 76% and 90% more candidate pairs on the ridge, and by the genotype truth that is wrong: kidney_nuc3 removed 1.45 times the true background (1.03 in round M2) with per-cell error 0.143 (0.116), kidney_nuc2 rank agreement 0.12 (0.22) and tubule markers removed from other cell types 78% (89%). Reading: related cell types express each other's genes weakly and in the proportions of the average cell, so in tissue the same line-up that marks swapped molecules in a cell-line mixture also marks weak expression. Whole-cell kidney is untouched (no depth-proportional background there).

0.4.0.dev9: the search for the swapped fraction is made only where the depth-proportional background is at most 5% of depth (swap_gate), and the bound is back at 5% (swap_cap); beyond the gate the depth-proportional background keeps the soup profile, as in 0.3.2. Swapped molecules are chimeric molecules, a few percent of a cell at most; 13 to 40% of a nucleus is ambient RNA it carries. The gate was set after seeing the two kidney nuclei libraries; it is a development decision and the confirmation libraries will have to bear it out. False-positive allowance in round M5: 0.4% gives same-species removal 1.08 of the extrapolated expectation and native loss 0.19%; 0.3% gives 1.00 and 0.13%; 0.2% gives 0.93 and 0.09%, with half a point less cross-species removal. Round M6: dev9 twice and once at 0.3%.

The benchmark's same-species truth is wrong on several libraries (code/benchmark/diag_species_split.py, raw data only). It multiplies each cell's cross-species counts by the species split of the empty partitions. Measured where the background is visible (human RNA in mouse cells against mouse RNA in human cells, each as a constant plus a share of depth), the split inside cells differs: hgmm_10k_v3 empty partitions 88% human, background inside cells 70% human, so the benchmark expects 3.2 times too much same-species background in human cells and a third of it in mouse cells (2.5 times too much over the library); jurkat_32d 1.75 times too little in human cells and 0.54 in mouse cells (1.33 times too little over the library); parse_hgmm_sub1 0.12 and 6.3. It agrees within 10% on hgmm_1k_v3, hgmm_10k_5pv2_ctrl, hgmm_12k_v2, bd_hgmm_mix1 and xeno_HSC_1, and within 25% on neat_barnyard. Against the measured split Glymph's same-species removal is 1.00 on hgmm_10k_v3 (0.40 by the benchmark's figure, a long-standing oddity) and 1.02 on jurkat_32d (1.36); CellBender 0.4.0 is at 0.80 and 0.33. species_mix_metrics.py now writes both versions (columns ending in _measured: the measured version assumes only that background does not depend on the species of the cell it lands in). The cross-species scores are not affected.

Per-cell look at the clusters that the rule for background-like clusters merged (code/benchmark/diag_merge_cells.py, dev7 outputs). The dirty cells of bd_hgmm_mix1 (82 cells, median 6% of the other species) are the upper tail of their parent's distribution: no gap (5th percentile of the cluster over 99th of the parent 1.45) and a wide spread inside (95th over 5th percentile 6.1). The other merged clusters on the cell-line mixtures are doublets (20 to 39% of the other species; spread 1.7 to 2.1). True populations are far apart (gap 10 to 56, spread 1.0). The same look at three tissue libraries is queued; if cell types there show a gap and a narrow spread, a continuity test could make the rule safe.

Round M6 scored (0.4.0.dev9; tables in metrics/). The gate works: kidney is back at the level of round M2 (per-cell error 0.0900 against 0.0893; removed over truth 1.06; rank agreement 0.382; CellBender 0.4.0: 0.0971, 0.96, 0.368) and the mixtures keep the gain (removal 91.5% against 90.7% in M2 and 83.4% for CellBender; two runs differ by 0.05 points on average). With a false-positive allowance of 0.3%: removal 91.3%, same-species removal 1.00 of the benchmark's expectation and 1.02 of the measured one, native loss 0.13%. With the same-species truth measured inside cells: per-cell error 0.0152 against CellBender's 0.0438 (lower on all 15 mixtures; hgmm_10k_v3 0.0080 against 0.047, where the benchmark's own figure had 0.048 against 0.047) and rank agreement 0.73 against 0.51 (higher on 13; CellBender is ahead on the two Parse cell-line sublibraries). Behind CellBender on cross-species removal on four mixtures, by 0.1 to 1.0 point (bd_hgmm_mix1, hgmm_1k_v3, hgmm_10k_5pv2_ctrl, hgmm_5k_v3).

The rule for background-like clusters cannot be made safe by a per-cell continuity test (code/benchmark/diag_merge_cells.py on dev9 outputs with --superpose). In kidney and fetal cortex the clusters it merges show the same signature as the dirty cells of the BD mixture: no gap to the larger cluster (0.1 to 1.3; BD 1.6) and a wide spread inside (95th over 5th percentile 3 to 12; BD 6.2). Cell states in tissue are continuous. The rule stays off and the BD mixture stays one point behind CellBender.

Frozen as 0.4.0rc1 for the confirmation run 20261118-2004_glymph-040rc1-bench: 0.4.0.dev9 with a false-positive allowance of 0.3% and the splicing step opt-in (--splice; it needs layers["unspliced"] and did not improve the kidney nuclei). In it: calibration clusters from principal components, the tree that only protects, the swapped fraction read from gene contrast where the depth-proportional background is at most 5% of depth. Built and off: first tree (tree_peel), level shared across clusters (silent_factor_max), background-like clusters (superpose), splicing (splice). Unit tests pass (job 59824975). Not committed.

The confirmation run of 0.4.0rc1 (20261118-2004_glymph-040rc1-bench) found a fit that runs away on bd_demo_pbmc: the pairs tested for the background level are those that expect enough background under the current fit, so a larger background makes more genes testable, the newcomers are weakly expressed genes above it, and they pull it up (1,000 to 1,800 tested pairs per cluster at the end, against 20 to 480 in 0.3.2; background 17% of depth; ambient multiplier at its lower bound). 0.3.2 fell into it from one of three starting clusterings and kept the middle estimate; clusters from principal components are nearly the same from every start, so all three fall in and the middle no longer protects. 0.4.0.dev10: the tested pairs are settled at the starting amounts (one empty-partition level per cell) and do not follow the fit (calib_fixed_candidates). Round M7: dev10 twice on the 23 development libraries and on bd_demo_pbmc, bd_spleen and bd_liver (looked at before, not held out, not in the earlier rounds), with the rc1 behaviour on those three for comparison. The development run is open again.

Round M7 read from the reports before its scores (code/benchmark/show_fit_health.py: background at the median depth as a share of depth, share of the called cells set aside, amounts at their bounds). Settling the tested pairs at the start cures bd_demo_pbmc (background 2.9% of depth; 17.2% when the pairs follow the fit; 3.7% in 0.3.2; cells set aside 0.1% against 28%) and breaks parse_bm_hfd the same way (34% of depth with the ambient multiplier at its lower bound and 7% of the cells set aside; 2.8% when the pairs follow the fit). On the other 24 libraries the two rules agree within a fifth. So the runaway is not a property of one rule: the lowest peak of observed over expected counts can stop qualifying as a peak (a tenth of the tallest) under either, and the level then climbs onto weakly expressed genes. 0.4.0.dev11: both rules are run from every starting clustering, each gives its middle estimate, and where the two differ by more than half the lower one is kept (calib_cross_check; otherwise the pairs follow the fit as in 0.4.0rc1). Expression can only add counts to genes taken for silent, so the lower of two disagreeing answers is the one that did not run away. Round M8: dev11 twice on the same 26 libraries.

Round M8 read from the reports (scores follow): with the cross-check the fits are those of 0.4.0rc1 on 25 of the 26 libraries, and bd_demo_pbmc is at 2.9% of depth (the rule settled at the start; 17.2% from the other). The two rules disagree on bd_demo_pbmc and on six of the eight sublibraries of parse_bm_hfd, where following the fit is the lower one and is kept. That library is not healthy under either rule: its sublibraries come out at 240 to 390 background counts at the median depth in four cases and near 2,000 in at least two, which cannot all be right for one tissue in one experiment. A known weak spot since 0.3.1 (Parse tissue), now located: the level can climb onto weakly expressed genes when the truly silent ones are too few to count as a peak.
